messages.subject: Instructions to advise — Hartwell Pharma v Tessaract Bioreagents
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Harriet,

We enclose by separate transfer our instructions to advise on the merits in Hartwell Pharma v Tessaract Bioreagents (CL-2026-000118). The three questions we'd value your view on: (1) liability for the defective batch; (2) whether clause 14.4 disapplies the £250k cap because the change-control breach was 'deliberate'; and (3) recoverability of the clinical-delay/standby head on remoteness.

Defence is awaited but the shape is clear from the LBA response. Grateful for a written advice and then a conference.

Tom

--
Whitfield Carter LLP, 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
Confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.subject: RE: Instructions to advise — Hartwell Pharma v Tessaract Bioreagents
messages.plaintextBody:
Tom, Sarah,

My written advice is attached. In short: liability is strong (~80%); the 'deliberate breach' construction point is the crux on the cap and I put us at 60-65% and likely to be appealed; the wasted-manufacturing and replacement heads are plainly recoverable, the clinical-delay head is more exposed but in my view recoverable given the purpose of the agreement. Good candidate for mediation while preparing firmly for trial. Happy to take it in conference next week.

Harriet
